excerpt: SafeBreach is a breach and attack simulation (BAS) and exposure validation platform that safely runs real attacker techniques against your defences. Founded in 2014; offices in Sunnyvale and Tel Aviv.
content:
SafeBreach makes security software that tests whether an organisation's defences actually stop attacks. Instead of waiting for a real breach or an annual penetration test, its platform continuously runs genuine but safe hacker behaviours against an organisation's security controls, then shows where they fall short and how to prioritise fixes. This category is known as breach and attack simulation (BAS). SafeBreach now describes its product as an exposure validation platform that combines BAS with attack path validation, and positions it for continuous threat exposure management (CTEM), including validating AI attack surfaces and AI-driven remediation. SecurityWeek reported in 2020 that its playbook contained more than 13,000 breach behaviours, and the company publishes research as its Hacker's Playbook.

SafeBreach was founded in 2014 by CEO Guy Bejerano and CTO Itzik Kotler, veterans of the Israeli Air Force and the IDF's Unit 8200 intelligence corps, according to Globes. The company has offices in Sunnyvale, California, and Tel Aviv. Its About page says the founders wanted to combine the mindset of a CISO with the toolset of a hacker.

SafeBreach raised a $15 million Series A in 2016 and a $15 million Series B in 2018. In April 2020 it closed a $19 million Series C led by OCV Partners, with Sequoia Capital, Deutsche Telekom Capital Partners, DNX Ventures, Hewlett Packard Pathfinder and PayPal participating, taking total funding past $50 million, SecurityWeek and Globes reported. In November 2021 it announced a $53.5 million Series D led by Sonae IM and Israel Growth Partners, which it said brought total funding to over $106 million. In April 2026 it launched an AI-powered CTEM product built around its Helm AI agent.

SafeBreach sells to enterprises through demos and does not publish prices. This profile draws on SafeBreach's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

profile.category: Breach and attack simulation / exposure validation
profile.platform: Enterprise security platform (cloud and on-premises simulators)
profile.summary_short: Continuously and safely simulates real attacks to test whether your security controls work

gallery.alt: SafeBreach homepage illustration of a white lunar-lander-style module with magenta windows, standing on four legs
Teal and blue graphic of concentric circles ringed with check marks over a blurred dashboard, from SafeBreach's Validate solution brief

use_cases: Testing whether firewalls, endpoint and email security actually block known attacks
Validating defences against a newly reported threat within days
Finding and prioritising attack paths an intruder could take
Running a continuous threat exposure management (CTEM) programme
Showing the board measurable evidence of security posture

fit: run a security team at a large enterprise with many security controls
want continuous evidence that defences work, not a yearly test
not_fit: are a small business without a dedicated security team
need application code scanning rather than control validation

alternatives.intro: Other breach and attack simulation and exposure validation tools. We have not compared them hands-on.

items.name: Pentera
items.difference: Emulates real attacks across the network in an automated pentest style.

items.name: AttackIQ
items.difference: Closely mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework.

items.what: Exposure management and security validation platform
items.difference: Like-for-like rival in BAS and CTEM.

faq.q: What is breach and attack simulation?
faq.a: Software that safely mimics real attacker techniques inside your environment to check whether your security controls detect and block them.
